rv.q: The sum of these parts is a challenging and engaging three hours spent in Wilson’s world.
Director Manny Buckley knows exactly what he's doing here, and he does it very well.
Buckley has crafted a sturdy take on this play that, despite occasional overplayed moments, mostly lands with sharply realized emotional truth in the smaller venue.
I King Hedley II is presented with competent, though ultimately forgettable, panache.
But “King Hedley II”—now playing at City Lit in a production whose moments of high intensity are dissipated in an unfocused, over-long staging—seems out of balance.
This is a production you're not going to want to miss.
Aside from the outstanding talented writing of August Wilson, his words come alive through the efforts of this terrific cast who leave it all on the stage.
City Lit brings the rich world of King Hedley II wonderfully to life- go see it!

cn.t: City Lit's intimate production of Wilson's drama earns strong praise for its gripping storytelling and powerful performances, particularly the intense, unpredictable central turn that anchors this exploration of family and consequence.
